title: fix(app-shell): the package permission door refuses the save when its re-read rejects (objectui#9420)
body:
Fixes #9420

## What was wrong

`PermissionMatrixEditPage.doSave`'s **package door** documents an ADR-0086 P0
guarantee in its own comment: merge only this package's slice back onto a fresh
read of the record, so rows contributed by other packages survive byte-for-byte.
The fresh read was `client.layered(...).catch(() => null)` and the merge base was
`fresh?.effective ?? payload`.

On the rejecting arm the guarantee **inverted**. `payload` is the editor's own
draft, which the load path already sliced down to this package's objects, so
`mergePermissionSlice` had no out-of-scope rows left to copy and the write PUT a
record with every other package's permission rows **deleted** — 200, no error, no
warning, on a security surface.

## What changed

A **rejected** re-read now refuses the save. Nothing is PUT, and the refusal
reaches the author on the page's **existing** error strip — the same `setError`
channel a failed `client.save` already renders into. No new toast path, no retry
added (the client offers no retry idiom at this call site, and a retry would
narrow the window rather than restore the guarantee). The rejection stays inside
`.catch`, so it can never escape as an unhandled one; the refusal is raised inside
`doSave`'s own `try` and caught by the handler that was already there.

One new i18n key, `perm.save.rereadFailed`, in both the `en` and `zh` tables of
the metadata-admin designer table.

### What is deliberately NOT refused — and why it matters

Only a **rejection** refuses. `MetadataClient.layered` resolves a **404** as
`{ effective: null, … }` rather than rejecting, and that arm keeps the
`?? payload` base on purpose: a set that exists only as a package draft — what the
Studio Access pillar's "+ New" creates, before any publish — has no published rows
for anyone to lose, and refusing there would make the first save of every newly
created permission set impossible. Pinned, so the refusal cannot widen onto it by
accident.

The **environment (whole-record) door** never took this path at all: with no
`packageId` there is no slice merge and no pre-save re-read. Pinned as a guard in
the same file — same client, same edit, same click, only `packageId` differs — and
it still PUTs the whole record with `force: false` and no draft options.

## Before / after — from the real run output, not an editor exit code

`PermissionMatrixEditor.packageDoorRereadRefusal.test.tsx` drives the REAL page
(load effect, real facet editors, real `doSave`) with `layered` resolving for the
load and rejecting for the save-time re-read.

**BEFORE** — the two production files reverted to `ff1d5ea8d` (the branch point)
with the new tests in place. `Test Files 1 failed | 2 passed (3)`,
`Tests 1 failed | 7 passed (8)`:

```
FAIL packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.packageDoorRereadRefusal.test.tsx
  > does NOT call client.save when the save-time layered re-read rejects
AssertionError: expected [ { name: 'sales_perms', …(3) } ] to deeply equal []

- []
+ [
+   {
+     "fields": {},
+     "label": "Sales",
+     "name": "sales_perms",
+     "objects": {
+       "a_account": {},
+     },
+   },
+ ]
```

That printed body **is** the card's one-shot probe, independently reproduced:
`objects` keys are `["a_account"]` alone, `fields` is empty, `b_order` and
`b_order.total` are gone.

**AFTER** — same six files, fix in place: `Test Files 6 passed (6)`,
`Tests 24 passed (24)`.

Mutation and restoration were both proved on disk rather than read off an editor's
exit code: the mutated file's `git hash-object` differed from its HEAD blob, the
removed text grepped to 0 occurrences, and after the restore `git status` was empty
and `git hash-object` matched the HEAD blob again for both files. The revert ran
against the committed fix, so the red and green numbers come from real trees.

## One sibling pin had to move, and it was measured rather than assumed

`PermissionMatrixEditor.readDecorationStrip.test.tsx` (landed with objectui#8181)
reached the `base = payload` fallback through the **rejected** re-read, and asserted
on the body that was PUT. This change removes that PUT, so its entrance no longer
exists. It was **not** weakened and **not** deleted: its subject, its assertions and
its controls are unchanged, and it now reaches the very same `?? payload` fallback
through the other entrance — the 404 shape described above, which `doSave` still
saves on.

Measured, so the retarget is not merely asserted: with the strip removed at the
unwrap (`stripReadDecorations(` count 1 to 0 on disk, blob hash changed), the
retargeted pin goes **red** with `expected { name: 'sales_perms', …(8) } to not have
property "_diagnostics"`, and it is green again after restore with the file byte
identical to its HEAD blob. It still fails for exactly the reason it was written.

`PermissionMatrixEditor.packageDoorFacets.test.tsx` — the arm the card names as
already holding — is untouched and green.

## Verification

Run from the repo root, in a dedicated worktree, all through the shared verify lock.

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run` over the six permission files | `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 24 passed (24)` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/` (the whole changed package) | `Test Files 703 passed (703)`, `Tests 6889 passed \| 1 skipped (6890)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` + `tsconfig.test.json`) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run lint` | exit 0, 0 errors, 3023 warnings (the package's standing warning baseline) |
| `check:i18n-keys` · `check:i18n-drift` · `check:i18n-dead-keys` · `check:i18n-designer-parity` | all exit 0 |
| `check:control-bytes` · `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 |
| `check-vi-mock-specifiers` · `check-vi-mock-inherit` · `check-vi-mock-override-shape` · `check-test-path-roots` | all exit 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence` · `check-changeset-no-major` · `check-changeset-overwrite` | all exit 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over this PR's five paths | NOT GOVERNED |

The dependency closure was built first (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`),
because an unbuilt closure makes `type-check` report sixteen phantom
`Cannot find module '@object-ui/…'` errors that say nothing about this diff.

## Acceptance notes

Noted while reading the code, **not** filed and **not** fixed here:

- The `?? payload` fallback has **two** entrances, and the card names only one.
  The second is a resolved-but-empty envelope (`effective` nullish), which is the
  404 shape. It is correct behaviour for a record the server does not hold, which
  is why it is kept — but the card's prose reads as though rejection were the only
  way in. Recorded here so the next reader of `doSave` does not re-derive it.
- The card and the claim comment both cite the guarantee docblock at
  `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:670`. On `ff1d5ea8d` that line is a *different*
  ADR-0086 P0 mention, inside `bulkSetObject`; the guarantee this PR is about sits
  in `doSave`, immediately above the merge. The two other cited lines (the `base`
  fallback and the `mergePermissionSlice` call) matched exactly. This is AGENTS.md
  commandment #11 demonstrating itself.
Filed rather than noted, because it is a reproducible defect in its own right:

- **objectui#9484** — at environment scope a rejected **post**-save `layered` read
  surfaces on the same error strip *after* a write that succeeded, and skips
  `resetDraftBaseline`, so the editor also keeps claiming unsaved changes for a
  record that is already persisted. Pre-existing, untouched by this PR (the ruling
  scoped this change to the package door), and reached by this PR's own
  environment-door guard test.

Serial constraint checked: objectui#7727 is `pm:dispatched` on the same directory
but on `ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx`. No overlap — this PR touches
`PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`, `i18n.ts` and two permission test files.

Clause-② stays **no**: nothing new is exported from `@object-ui/app-shell`, no
published type moved, no authoring surface widened. `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/index.ts`
is not touched, and `permission-slice.ts` was read-only throughout — the refusal
belongs to the caller that chooses the merge base, not to the merge itself.
